investigacion.base:
The World Series hasn't started yet, so the question can't be resolved today (Oct 19, 2026). Its Game 6 is scheduled for Oct 30.

**Resolution sources**
- **Baseball-Reference 2026 WS page:** I couldn't load it in my search results. Because the series starts Oct 23, it can't have any game results yet.
- **Metaculus FAQ "credible sources":** This is just a definition (reputable outlets can be used if Baseball-Reference isn't available). It doesn't change anything here.

**Where things stand**
- **Brewers:** They won a franchise-record 103 games in the regular season, leading the Majors in wins for a second straight season. They took down the Padres in four games in the NLDS and then swept the Dodgers in the NLCS. They clinched on Thursday, Oct 15, and will be well rested for Game 1 of the World Series with a week off in between games. They have home-field advantage.
- **ALCS:** On Oct 18, the Rays defeated the Guardians 3-1 in Game 5 to take a 3-2 series lead, behind seven strong innings from Drew Rasmussen. Game 6 is Monday, Oct. 19, 8 p.m. at Tropicana Field, and a Game 7 would also be in Tampa. A Friday rainout means the ALCS could run four games in four straight days if the ALCS goes the full distance. So the AL team's pitching staff will be more worn down than Milwaukee's.
- **Betting odds (ESPN, about Oct 17; I found no volume data, and these are sportsbook lines, not a prediction market):** Milwaukee Brewers -170 Cleveland Guardians +330 Tampa Bay Rays +475. These were posted when Cleveland led the ALCS 2-1 and are now out of date. The -170 line means roughly a 60–63% chance of the Brewers winning the series, which works out to about 56% per game. I didn't find any Polymarket or Kalshi market on series length.

**Schedule ([MLB.com](https://www.mlb.com/news/2026-mlb-playoff-and-world-series-schedule))**
- Games 1 and 2: Oct 23–24 in Milwaukee
- Games 3, 4 and 5 (if needed): Oct 26–28 at the AL champion's park
- Game 6 (if needed): Friday, Oct. 30 ALCS winner @ Brewers, Game 6: 8 p.m.
- Game 7 (if needed): Oct 31

**Base rates**
- **Math model:** If every game were a coin flip, the chance of a Game 6 is 1 − P(sweep) − P(5 games) = 1 − 0.125 − 0.25 = 62.5%. If one team wins 56% of games, it's about 60%. At 60%, it's about 58%. At 65%, it's about 53%.
- **History:** These figures are from memory and may be slightly off. Of the roughly 115 best-of-seven World Series, about 21 were sweeps and about 27 went five games, so about 55–58% reached a Game 6.
- **Recent series:** 2019 went 7 games, 2020 went 6, 2021 went 6, 2022 went 6, 2023 went 5 (TEX–ARI), 2024 went 5 (LAD–NYY), and 2025 went 7 (LAD–TOR). That's 5 of the last 7.

**Things to consider**
- A strong favorite, the long Brewers rest, and a tired AL opponent could make a short series more likely.
- On the other hand, the Rays' Rasmussen is in top form, and too much rest has sometimes hurt teams in the past.
- The ALCS winner will be known after tonight's game or Game 7 on Oct 20.

criterios: This question resolves YES if a Game 6 is played in the 2026 Major League Baseball World Series between the Milwaukee Brewers and the American League champion (the winner of the Guardians–Rays ALCS). Game 6 is scheduled for Friday, October 30, 2026. A Game 6 is required (and thus played) only if neither team has won four games after the first five games — i.e., the series stands at 3 games to 2 after Game 5. The question resolves NO if the series is decided in four or five games, so that no sixth game is necessary. Resolution is based on the official 2026 World Series results page at Baseball-Reference (https://www.baseball-reference.com/postseason/2026_WS.shtml), or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) if that page is unavailable.
letra_pequena: If the World Series is canceled or shortened such that no Game 6 can occur, the question resolves NO. A Game 6 that is scheduled and officially begins but is later suspended or postponed still counts as a Game 6 being played, resolving YES.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** The need for Game 6 should be known after Game 5, scheduled for October 28—about nine days from today.

(b) **Status quo:** The World Series has not started. Game 6 is on the schedule only *if needed*, so there is no current series result to carry forward.

(c) **Reference class:** Roughly 55–60% of historical best-of-seven World Series have reached Game 6. An evenly matched series would do so 62.5% of the time; Milwaukee’s apparent edge lowers that estimate somewhat.

(d) **No scenario:** Either team wins four of the first five games.

(e) **Yes scenario:** After five games, one team leads 3–2, and Game 6 begins.

(f) **Technicality:** A Game 6 that officially begins counts even if suspended later. A canceled or shortened World Series in which it cannot occur resolves No.

**Probability: 60%**

(a) **Time left:** About 11 days until the scheduled Game 6 on October 30; a four- or five-game series would settle the question sooner.

(b) **Status quo:** The World Series has not started. Game 6 is on the schedule, but only if needed.

(c) **Reference class:** Roughly 55–60% of historical best-of-seven World Series have reached Game 6. An evenly matched series would do so 62.5% of the time; Milwaukee’s favored status lowers that estimate somewhat.

(d) **No scenario:** Either team wins the series 4–0 or 4–1.

(e) **Yes scenario:** The teams split the first five games 3–2, requiring Game 6.

(f) **Technicality:** Game 6 counts as played if it officially begins, even if later suspended or postponed. A cancellation that prevents it from occurring resolves No.

**Probability: 60%**

(a) **Time left:** The World Series starts October 23. Whether a Game 6 is needed will be known after Game 5 on October 28, about 9 days from now. Game 6 itself is October 30.

(b) **Status quo:** Nothing has been played yet, so there is no status quo outcome. The prior comes from the structure of a best-of-seven series and from history.

(c) **Reference class and base rate:**
- **History:** Of about 115 best-of-seven World Series, roughly 55–58% reached a Game 6. Five of the last seven did.
- **Model:** Suppose the Brewers win about 56–58% of games. That is consistent with the stale −170 series price, given that the AL opponent is now likely the Rays, who lead the ALCS 3-2.
  - At p = 0.58, a sweep has about a 14.4% chance and a five-game series about 26.2%.
  - That gives about a 59% chance of a Game 6.
  - A stronger favorite (about 62% per game) would push it toward about 55%.

(d) **No scenario:** The well-rested Brewers beat a tired AL champion that just played a long ALCS. They take both home games and finish the series in Game 4 or 5 on the road.

(e) **Yes scenario:** The teams split games, as is typical in roughly even matchups. The series stands 3-2 after Game 5 and returns to Milwaukee on October 30.

(f) **Technicalities:**
- If Game 6 officially begins and is then suspended or postponed, it counts as YES.
- If the series is cancelled or shortened, it resolves NO, but that is negligible.
- A rainout only shifts dates; a Game 6 played on a later date still counts.
- In practice, the question reduces to whether the series is 3-2 after five games.

Both history and the model put the answer in the high 50s. The Brewers' edge in rest and the AL team's pitching fatigue shave it slightly.

Probability: 57%
